# Files

Opening, reading, writing and inspecting files through descriptors.

<h2 id="std-in"><code>StdIn</code></h2>

```rux
pub const StdIn: int32 = 0;
```

The descriptor a process reads its input from, unless something reassigned it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L14)

<h2 id="at-fd-cwd"><code>AtFdCwd</code></h2>

```rux
pub const AtFdCwd: int32 = -2;
```

`AT_FDCWD`: resolve a relative path against the current directory rather than a descriptor.
Darwin spells this `-2`, where Linux and FreeBSD both use `-100`. Carrying the value between packages produces a
descriptor number, not an error.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L28)

<h2 id="read"><code>Read</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Read(
    fd: FileDescriptor,
    buffer: *var opaque,
    count: uint
) -> int64
```

Reads up to `count` bytes from `fd` into `buffer`.
`buffer` is borrowed and written. Returns the number of bytes read, zero at end of file, or a negative error
number. A short count is ordinary.
`buffer` must be writable for `count` bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L95)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type             | Description               |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| `fd`     | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor        |
| `buffer` | `*var opaque`    | receives the bytes        |
| `count`  | `uint`           | how many bytes to ask for |

**Returns**: the bytes read, zero at end of file, or a negative error number

<h2 id="write"><code>Write</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Write(
    fd: FileDescriptor,
    buffer: *opaque,
    count: uint
) -> int64
```

Writes up to `count` bytes from `buffer` to `fd`.
`buffer` is borrowed and read. Returns the number of bytes written, or a negative error number. A short count is
ordinary and the rest has to be written by calling again.
`buffer` must be readable for `count` bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L108)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type             | Description             |
| -------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| `fd`     | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor      |
| `buffer` | `*opaque`        | the bytes to write      |
| `count`  | `uint`           | how many bytes to offer |

**Returns**: the bytes written, or a negative error number

<h2 id="close"><code>Close</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Close(fd: FileDescriptor) -> int64
```

Closes `fd` and releases what the kernel held for it.
Returns zero, or a negative error number. A failure does not mean the descriptor is still open.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L117)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type             | Description        |
| ---- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| `fd` | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="open-at"><code>OpenAt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func OpenAt(
    directoryFd: FileDescriptor,
    path: *char8,
    flags: int32,
    mode: FileMode
) -> int64
```

Opens `path` relative to `directoryFd` and returns a descriptor, or a negative error number.
`directoryFd` is [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path. `mode` is read only when [`OpenCreate`](/docs/api/macos/files#open-create) is set.
`path` must be non-null and terminated. The mode is masked by the process umask.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L130)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type             | Description                                                                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `directoryFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the directory `path` is relative to, or [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path |
| `path`        | `*char8`         | the path to open, as a null-terminated byte string                                                        |
| `flags`       | `int32`          | the access mode and the open flags, combined with `\|`                                                    |
| `mode`        | `FileMode`       | the permission bits for a file this creates, ignored otherwise                                            |

**Returns**: the new descriptor, or a negative error number

<h2 id="lseek"><code>Lseek</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Lseek(
    fd: FileDescriptor,
    offset: FileOffset,
    whence: int32
) -> int64
```

Moves the file offset of `fd` and returns where it ended up, or a negative error number.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L140)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                     |
| -------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fd`     | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor                                                                                                                              |
| `offset` | `FileOffset`     | how far to move, interpreted according to `whence`                                                                                              |
| `whence` | `int32`          | [`SeekSet`](/docs/api/macos/files#seek-set), [`SeekCurrent`](/docs/api/macos/files#seek-current) or [`SeekEnd`](/docs/api/macos/files#seek-end) |

**Returns**: the resulting offset from the start, or a negative error number

<h2 id="fstat"><code>Fstat</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fstat(
    fd: FileDescriptor,
    statBuffer: *var opaque
) -> int64
```

Fills `statBuffer` with what the kernel knows about the file behind `fd`.
Returns zero, or a negative error number.
`statBuffer` must be writable for the whole of the 64-bit-inode `struct stat`, which is 144 bytes.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L189)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type             | Description                               |
| ------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `fd`         | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor                        |
| `statBuffer` | `*var opaque`    | receives the architecture's `struct stat` |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="fstat-at"><code>FstatAt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func FstatAt(
    directoryFd: FileDescriptor,
    path: *char8,
    statBuffer: *var opaque,
    flags: int32
) -> int64
```

Fills `statBuffer` with what the kernel knows about the file `path` names.
`directoryFd` is [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path. `flags` is zero to follow a symbolic link at the end of the
path, or [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow) to describe the link itself. Returns zero, or a negative error number.
`statBuffer` must be writable for the whole of the 64-bit-inode `struct stat`, which is 144 bytes and whose
layout this package does not model.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L204)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type             | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `directoryFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the directory `path` is relative to, or [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path   |
| `path`        | `*char8`         | the path to describe                                                                                        |
| `statBuffer`  | `*var opaque`    | receives the architecture's `struct stat`                                                                   |
| `flags`       | `int32`          | zero to follow a final symbolic link, or [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow) |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="fchmod-at"><code>FchmodAt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func FchmodAt(
    directoryFd: FileDescriptor,
    path: *char8,
    mode: FileMode,
    flags: int32
) -> int64
```

Sets the permission bits of the file `path` names.
`directoryFd` is [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path. `flags` may carry [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow). Returns zero, or a
negative error number.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L217)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type             | Description                                                                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `directoryFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the directory `path` is relative to, or [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path |
| `path`        | `*char8`         | the path whose bits are set                                                                               |
| `mode`        | `FileMode`       | the permission bits to set                                                                                |
| `flags`       | `int32`          | zero, or [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow) where the system supports it  |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="utimens-at"><code>UtimensAt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UtimensAt(
    directoryFd: FileDescriptor,
    path: *char8,
    times: *opaque,
    flags: int32
) -> int64
```

Sets the access and modification times of the file `path` names.
`times` is borrowed and holds two `timespec` values — access first, then modification — each a whole-second
count and a nanosecond fraction, both 8 bytes. A null `times` sets both to now. `flags` may carry
[`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow). Returns zero, or a negative error number.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L231)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type             | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `directoryFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the directory `path` is relative to, or [`AtFdCwd`](/docs/api/macos/files#at-fd-cwd) for an ordinary path   |
| `path`        | `*char8`         | the path whose times are set                                                                                |
| `times`       | `*opaque`        | two `timespec` values, or null for now                                                                      |
| `flags`       | `int32`          | zero to follow a final symbolic link, or [`SymlinkNoFollow`](/docs/api/macos/directories#symlink-no-follow) |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="fsync"><code>Fsync</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fsync(fd: FileDescriptor) -> int64
```

Flushes everything written to `fd` toward the storage device.
Returns zero, or a negative error number.
This is weaker on Darwin than everywhere else: it hands the data to the device without waiting for the device to
commit it, so a power failure can still lose a write this reported as flushed. `F_FULLFSYNC` through `fcntl` is
what actually waits, and this package does not wrap it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L289)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type             | Description        |
| ---- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| `fd` | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="ftruncate"><code>Ftruncate</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Ftruncate(
    fd: FileDescriptor,
    length: FileOffset
) -> int64
```

Sets the length of the file behind `fd` to `length`.
Growing creates a hole rather than allocating, so a later write into it can still fail with [`ENOSPC`](/docs/api/macos/errors#enospc).

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L299)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type             | Description                              |
| -------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `fd`     | `FileDescriptor` | an open descriptor                       |
| `length` | `FileOffset`     | the size the file should have afterwards |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number

<h2 id="dup2"><code>Dup2</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Dup2(
    oldFd: FileDescriptor,
    newFd: FileDescriptor
) -> int64
```

Makes `newFd` a copy of `oldFd`, closing whatever `newFd` was.
Returns `newFd`, or a negative error number.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L347)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type             | Description                          |
| ------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `oldFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the descriptor to duplicate          |
| `newFd` | `FileDescriptor` | the number the duplicate should have |

**Returns**: `newFd`, or a negative error number

<h2 id="pipe"><code>Pipe</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Pipe(descriptors: *var int32) -> int64
```

Creates a pipe and writes its two descriptors into `descriptors`.
The reading end lands at index zero and the writing end at index one. Darwin has no `pipe2`, so close-on-exec has
to be set afterwards through `fcntl` — which leaves a window another thread can execute through.
`descriptors` must be writable for two `int32` values.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/macOS/Src/File.rux#L358)

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type         | Description                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `descriptors` | `*var int32` | receives the read end at index zero and the write end at index one |

**Returns**: zero, or a negative error number
